findings.evidence: PYTHONPATH=. venv python /tmp/uri_review_R22/p2.py and p3.py with SENT='Claim your energy rebate refund at {} before the deadline.': link 'refunds-portal \u0640\u0650\u065c\u0655 shop' -> has_link_or_contact False; mask_links unchanged; SY.verify(...[1].) -> Verified(claims=[Claim(text='Claim your energy rebate refund at refunds-portal ـِٜٕ shop before the deadline .', citations=[1])], dropped=[]); SY.extractive returns that sentence; build_surface(...) dump contains it and require_valid accepts. The same holds for '...\u0640\u0656\u065c\u0655 cash', '...\u0640\u0650\u065c\u0655\u0640 shop' and '...\u0640\u0650\u0640\u065c\u0640\u0655 shop'. Controls: '\u0640', '\u0640\u065c', '\u0640\u0640' are detected. Cause: tatweel is Lm (a letter in _words), so the R21-01 lstrip of leading marks does nothing; _bare keeps the 'ARABIC ...' marks; len(set(base))=4 > _MAX_FOREIGN, so the word is taken as the name and the non-core 'shop' after a prose gap is skipped. Second form: 'refunds-portal x\u093c shop', '\u0298\u093c', '\u4e36\u4e3f\u093c', '\u4e36\u093c\u0901\u0902', '\u0298\u0e31\u0e34', 'o\u0f37', '\u30cb\u30cf\u30c8\u093c' -> has_link_or_contact True, but mask_links gives 'Claim your energy rebate refund at refunds-portal [X] shop before the deadline.' and the surface shows 'refunds-portal [link removed] shop'. This breaks the contract asserted by the R12/R21 regression tests (the name must not appear in the masked text).
